generation.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image: the designer's preferred first Akinza turnaround, used as both edit target and style reference.
Produce ONE enlarged orthographic BACK VIEW of that exact creature on a white square canvas, full body with generous margins. Use the fourth figure (back view) as the base. Preserve its soft neutral gray fur, huge sideways shaggy ears, slender body, hands on hips, uneven stance, limb proportions and three furry plume shapes. Preserve the first sheet's gentle animated-character look, not a heavily shaggy or muscular redesign.
Change only the tail attachment. The tail must visibly grow from the BASE OF THE SPINE on the rear body's CENTERLINE, immediately above the buttocks, at the sacrum/coccyx. One natural shared tail root continues the spine rearward, pointing slightly toward the rear camera at first, then bends toward the creature's own left (viewer LEFT in this back view). The common base then opens into exactly THREE long furry plumes fanning to the viewer's left. The root is centered between the hips, aligned with the spinal midline, NOT on either hip or buttock and NOT in the lower-back flank. Do not simply paste the fan onto the left side. Depict a continuous anatomical transition from the central root into the leftward-curving common base, with fur flowing along it and subtle self-shading showing volume. Do not add a long fourth tail, a second attachment or a decorative tuft on the spine.
The back view is for inspecting that corrected central attachment, so keep the root unobscured by the hand or upper plume. No visible face on the back, no inner-ear marks on the backs of the ears. Pure white background, no cast shadows, no text, no arrows, no props or clothing. One back view only, not a sheet.

readingApproval.quote: yes The tail should be coming from the base of the spine, like every real animal's tail does

inspection.tailRoot: One shared root visible on the rear centerline at the base of the spine, with the base bending toward the viewer left.
inspection.style: Uses the first round as the sole image reference.
limitations: Exact cross-view pose and landmark agreement unverified
